setup_failure: Initial calibrator filename profile.py shadowed a standard Python module; renamed before any model data was collected. The failure log is retained.
parallelism: After the first parallel launch, Llama made very slow progress. Qwen training was briefly paused with SIGSTOP, all Llama threads were moved to physical cores0-3, and Qwen resumed on4-7. Both processes preserve their tensors, seeds, and optimizer state. Initial direct-Llama config cpus records launch affinity4-7; subsequent affinity commands and timestamps are retained in logs. This is not a performance benchmark. No cache-fidelity measurements overlap these jobs; AMD fidelity begins after both complete.
worker_affinity_correction: A later check found all active Qwen classifier workers scheduled on CPU4 despite allowed range4-7. Explicit per-thread CPU4/5/6/7 affinities restored progress without changing tensors, seeds, optimizer state, or scientific parameters. The exact commands are retained in qwen-explicit-worker-affinity.log.
llama_classifier_affinity: Llama classifier main and three active workers were pinned to physical cores0/1/2/3 after epoch5, preserving optimizer state. Commands are archived in llama-classifier-worker-affinity.log; no fidelity measurements overlap training.
amd_qwen_quiet_repeat: The initial AMD Qwen cache acquisition briefly overlapped an outbound archive copy of completed Llama classifier artifacts; the initial synthetic controls ended near this copy boundary. Before examining any AMD cache metrics, both controls and Qwen were designated for complete identical-settings repeats after the Llama acquisition ends, with no concurrent artifact copies. Initial full raw runs are retained as diagnostics/amd-controls-before-quiet-repeat and diagnostics/amd-qwen-during-artifact-copy. Quiet repeats are primary regardless of outcome. Llama cache collection began after the outbound copy had finished; it is retained. Classifier training never overlapped cache acquisition.
